payload.claim: TRUST-BOUNDARY AUDIT 2026-09-24: 207/207 unit tests and 8/8 invariants pass while ALL TEN adversarial paths are open. The invariant suite is 8 unittest modules (38 tests) run by subprocess (brain/invariants.py:21) over the happy path only - it is the same epistemic class as the unit tests, NOT a boundary proof. Repro scripts: /tmp/brain-audit/probes.sh probes2.sh (ran against a sandbox copy, real vault untouched).

IDENTITY IS A CLI FLAG, NOT A CREDENTIAL. brain/cli.py:52 _agent() returns --agent verbatim, else $BRAIN_AGENT, else 'unknown'. So BRAIN_AGENT=opencode brain start --agent codex succeeds (A1). Every downstream control - leases, handoffs, closure_target, message .from, receipt .session_id - inherits this spoofable identity. This single hole negates topology, closure contract and evidence attribution at once.

TOPOLOGY IS FAIL-OPEN IN FOUR WAYS. (1) brain/dispatch.py:170 - the can_route check only runs when $BRAIN_AGENT is set, so unsetting it skips enforcement entirely; (2) brain/topology.py:132-137 - an undeclared source or target is permitted ('permissive for undeclared agents'), so opting out of the graph is the escape hatch; (3) brain/topology.py:126 - no topology.yaml means fully permissive, and only the 'second-brain' workspace has one - global (the DEFAULT workspace), jarvis and titan have none; (4) paths.py:235 BRAIN_BYPASS=1 is ungated and unaudited. Genuine denials do work when a declared seat routes to a declared seat (B9: codex->agy correctly refused).

COMPLETION GATE IS SELF-SATISFYING. brain/evidence.py:221-226 returns ok=True for ANY card whose latest session has target_agent in REVIEWER_ROLES - and target_agent is whatever the builder typed on brain end. Proven: a card reached [done] with zero receipts, closure=handed_off, on the string 'pytest: 999 passed' (B1). brain record-evidence --exit-code 0 writes a 'machine receipt' whose hashes are of caller-supplied strings (B2/A7); a hand-written receipts/rcpt_forged.json is accepted verbatim (C3); verify_task reads only receipts[0] so one old exit-0 receipt passes forever; transcript_sha256 is computed once at record time and never re-verified, so editing the log afterwards is undetectable (A9). INV-002 passes only because its tests omit the target_agent branch.

TWO EXECUTION/INTEGRITY ESCAPES. (1) brain test --cmd-text runs subprocess.run(shell=True) on any agent-supplied string with no lease or identity check (evidence.py:124-131) - proven to write outside the workspace (A8); git commit --no-verify skips the session hook with no audit (B8). (2) check_working_tree whitelists every path starting with workspaces/ (evidence.py:183) - which is where ALL brain records live - so hand-editing another agent's task card, session or receipt is invisible to the integrity gate (B7); and lease matching is suffix-based, f.endswith(l) or l.endswith(f) (evidence.py:188), so a lease on 'a.py' authorises 'src/deep/a.py' (A10). Guard also permits leasing meta/topology.yaml and another agent's session file (B5/B6). board.move overwrites task agent with no ownership check - claude re-assigned a card while opencode's session was still active (C1).

WORKING AS CLAIMED: file-lease conflict refusal is real (claude refused engine.py held by opencode, C2); directed inbox/outbox messaging works and survives restarts (messaging.py); the closure contract does require a legitimate reason and a closure_target (board.py:306-335); the global git pre-commit hook does block commits with no active session; the topology cycle/edge validator is sound. Fixes should preserve these.

HOOK CROSS-VAULT LEAK: the global post-commit hook (~/.config/git/hooks/post-commit) calls brain post with no vault resolution, so commits in ANY repo on this machine write into the default vault - an unrelated sandbox repo leaked a 10KB record into workspaces/second-brain/context/ (quarantined to meta/quarantine/). It also stamps --agent $(whoami), i.e. attribution to 'h00939', which is not a seat and so also gets permissive routing. Bind the hook to the repo's own vault and to a real seat.

payload.claim: A flag that opens a gate must cost the same authority as the gate: board.move(--force) bypassed INV-002 for any process that could type it, because --force was treated as a UI option instead of the break-glass. It now spends a witness-minted grant, so an agent cannot force its own card to done.

Custody of a record must include who the record already names. A seat may always speak for itself, so an unowned-by-nobody check let gemini move opencode's reviewed card and become its recorded author; the rule is now one function (board.may_speak_for) applied to the claimant, the credited worker and the existing author, with custody beginning at review/done so an expired lease cannot freeze the board.

Never let a caller name the directory an integrity check judges: evidence.check_working_tree accepted a caller-supplied cwd, so pointing it at any clean git tree reported a real unleased change as absent — and a cwd *below* the repo root reported the whole workspace clean because the subdirectory is not a repository. The workspace registration now picks the tree; cwd only has to be inside it.

An execution receipt that lets the writer name an arbitrary session_id is evidence laundering: any seat could file a passing run under another seat's session, or attach its own run from an unrelated card. record_receipt now refuses a session it does not belong to and a session working a different task (EVIDENCE_ATTRIBUTION_REFUSED).

The break-glass path is the least tested code on the machine and fails silently in both directions: every grant was unreadable (witness wrote it 0600), every genuine grant verified as forged (find() injected a _path key into the signed record), and every gate raised TypeError (the bypass() keyword spend shadowed the module's spend()). 259 unit tests were green through all three. Anything an agent must use in an emergency needs a probe, not a comment.

A privileged allow-list that matches basenames is not an allow-list: the witness normalised argv[0] to its basename, so a shim at /tmp/x/pytest was a root-sealed, root-observed exit code for code any agent wrote. Resolution must go through the same PATH the child gets, and compare realpaths; commands that exit 0 without exercising anything (--help, --version, --collect-only) are not evidence either.

Deleting the approval is not the same as having none: topology.load() only refused a *drifted* pin, so rm meta/topology.pin.json returned an agent its own edited routing graph. Under installed trust an un-pinned topology is now a hard error; in bootstrap it still loads, because nothing there is verifiable anyway.
